items.title: Gold heads for steep weekly loss as oil prices fuel Fed rate concerns
items.excerpt: Published Fri, Oct 23 2026 12:29 AM EDT ... Gold eased on Friday, headed for its steepest weekly decline in over four months as elevated oil prices bolstered higher-for-longer interest rate expectations, while investors awaited next week's Federal Reserve policy meet. Chalinee Thirasupa | ... Gold eased on Friday, headed for its steepest weekly decline in over four months as elevated oil prices bolstered higher-for-longer interest rate expectations, while investors awaited next week's Federal Reserve policy meet. ... Speculators are trying to defend the key $4,000 level for gold because a clean break below would signal that the market has stopped pricing rate relief and started pricing sticky inflation, elevated yields, and a stronger dollar, said Monte Safieddine, head of market research at Capital.com. Oil prices rose about 4% to a five-month high on Thursday after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies. Elevated energy prices bolster expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates by the Fed, increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. "Any further escalation on the geopolitical front risks pushing oil even higher. Higher oil is reviving inflation fears, lifting yields, and delaying Fed easing. That is a difficult cocktail for bullion," Safieddine added. ... Focus has turned to the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting and next week's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, a closely watched gauge as it is the central bank's preferred inflation measure as it targets a 2% inflation rate. Traders are largely expecting the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged next week, but expectations for an interest rate hike in December remain at 80%.

items.title: Senate control hinges on unwanted nominees
items.excerpt: Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) are living out their midterm nightmares — with nominees they didn't want and former colleagues they no longer control. Why it matters: Together, Schumer and Thune are stuck with five Senate races in which their party establishments thought they had a better chance of winning with someone else. - 🤠 Texas: Thune's efforts to stop Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton from winning the party's Senate nomination failed. Now Republicans are spending more than $329 million to defeat state Rep. James Talarico— and it's still a nail-biter. - 🍑 Georgia: GOP leaders couldn't convince Gov. Brian Kemp to run. The eventual nominee, Rep. Mike Collins, has struggled to keep pace with fundraising juggernaut Sen. Jon Ossoff (D). GOP money is in retreat. - 🦞 Maine: Schumer endorsed Gov. Janet Mills, but Graham Platner's implosion left Democrats with backup Troy Jackson against Sen. Susan Collins. - ⛴️ Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens and made a name for himself nationally. But he won by just one point even though primary polls showed him up by double digits. He's now polling within the margin of error against the GOP nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers. - 🏈 Minnesota: Peggy Flanagan ran as a progressive, said she would not support Schumer as leader and bested establishment-backed Rep. Angie Craig. But Cook Political Report moved her race against former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya toward Republicans even as it shifted other races toward Democrats.

items.title: Justice Department asks appeals court to intervene in California ballot case
items.excerpt: Oct. 23, 2026, 12:22 AM EDT / Source: Reuters ... The Justice Department asked an appeals court Thursday to intervene in its lawsuit seeking to temporarily block California from counting more than 20,000 mail-in ballots from voters the Trump administration says are likely not U.S. citizens. The Justice Department asked the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to get involved before a lower-court judge ruled in the dispute. Justice Department lawyers said the unusual maneuver was necessary because the judge assigned to the case, U.S. District Judge David Carter, had not made a decision by Thursday afternoon, as the department had requested. Carter scheduled a hearing for next week to consider the department’s request for an emergency order to block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 voters in the Nov. 3 midterm elections until their citizenship status could be verified. The department said it interpreted Carter’s lack of ruling as a “constructive denial” of its request. The case is being closely watched as the Trump administration seeks to exert greater control over the elections next month that will determine control of Congress. The Justice Department is considering bringing litigation against more states as part of its efforts to remove noncitizens from voter rolls ahead of the midterms, a department official previously told NBC News. ... Democratic Party leaders have sued in federal court to block the Trump administration from overriding state authority to administer elections or intimidate state and local election officials.

At least 60 people have also died in ICE custody since January 2025. ... That track record has made democracy advocates and human rights groups worried about ICE’s activities in the lead-up to the November 3 midterm elections. Organisations like Human Rights Watch and the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) have voiced concern that the Trump administration could use ICE to intimidate voters. The threat of encountering ICE agents could also keep some voters away from the ballot box, the groups say. One national poll, conducted in September by the University of California, San Diego, found that 40 percent of respondents expected ICE agents to be present near polling stations on election day. ... Federal law prohibits the use of armed federal agents at polling stations. Some states have similar provisions. ... Only US citizens are allowed to vote in federal elections. Starting in August, the Department of Homeland Security deployed HSI agents for “field investigations” in at least nine states to probe questions of voter eligibility. Some have reportedly gone door to door, asking residents if they are citizens and if they plan to vote. ... items.excerpt: ## Music and entertainment news from Australia and around the world, plus new releases and tour updates. US rock giants Bon Jovi are returning to Australia in 2027 for live shows in support of the band’s latest album ‘Forever’. Bon Jovi play Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium on 4 March and Sydney’s Accor Stadium on 11 March, their first Australian shows since 2018. Spotify has removed more than 75 million tracks from its platform as part of an ongoing crackdown on AI-generated spam and low-quality music. The streaming giant says the purge is aimed at curbing mass uploads designed to manipulate recommendations and royalty payments, while protecting legitimate artists and listeners. The move highlights the growing challenge facing music platforms as generative AI makes it easier to produce and distribute tracks at scale. Carol Choi will soon succeed Luke Kang as president of The Walt Disney Company’s Asia Pacific operations, overseeing the entertainment giant’s business across the region, including Australia and New Zealand. The leadership transition places Choi at the helm of Disney’s regional strategy as the company continues to develop its film, television and streaming operations in key Asia Pacific markets. ... Swedish-Argentinian singer-songwriter José González has announced an Australian tour next year for his fifth studio album ‘Against The Dying Of The Light’, which was released in March. González plays Adelaide, Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne in February 2027.

items.title: LISA, Miley & Kacey Musgraves Lead Best New Music: Friday Music Guide
items.excerpt: LISA, Miley & Kacey Musgraves Lead Best New Music: Friday Music Guide 10/23/2026 ... This week, LISA drops her new EP; Miley features two new songs on the Nobody Wants This season three soundtrack; Kacey Musgraves shares a taste of her just-announced Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes; and John Mayer is back with a new single and newly-launched label… plus much more. Check out all of this week’s picks below: LISA, Press Play Led by the hard-hitting pop-rap single “SaWaDiKa,” released in September, LISA is now sharing her very first solo EP. Focus track “Tarantino” packs just as hard a punch, while “Cobra” is an attitude-packed dance-pop song and album closer “Sweat” is a sultry song that leaves its subject with a simple instruction — “don’t stress me out” — and its listener wanting more. Press Play follows the 2025 release of LISA’S debut solo full-length, Alter Ego, and arrives just in time for the Thai singer’s upcoming Vegas residency that kicks off in November. — LYNDSEY HAVENS ... Miley, “Cold Blooded” For longtime Miley fans, the release of “Cold Blooded” has been a long time coming. Written in the late 2010s ahead of her EP She Is Coming, the track never saw the light of day — until now. A demo version of the ballad, which showcases Miley’s undeniable vocal control and power over simple piano chords, is featured as a bonus track on the season three soundtrack for Nobody Wants This, out today. Its one of two Miley demos that made it on the album, as a stripped-down version of her Endless Summer Vacation track “You” also features on the soundtrack and in an episode. The soundtrack is out on Atlantic, while all 10 episodes of season three are now streaming on Netflix. — L. H. Kacey Musgraves, “Weekend In Texas” Kacey Musgraves is previewing her upcoming project Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes (out Jan. 15 on Lost Highway Records) with the release of new music, including “Weekend In Texas.” “I’ve got the hat and the cattle to back it up / Everything will be great in my favorite state of mind,” she sings. Bright horns, an irresistible groove and Musgraves’ dulcet vocal tones blend luxuriously as she sings of longing for a soul-restoring few days of escape in the Lone Star State. This new release feels both classic and invigorating. — JESSICA NICHOLSON ... John Legend, Muse After linking up with Clipse and Pharrell Williams for the Let God Sort Em Out standout “The Birds Don’t Sing,” John Legend linked up with the Oscar-nominated production powerhouse for Muse, their first full album together after 20 years of friendship. Primarily written and recorded at Williams’ Louis Vuitton HQ studio in Paris, the two superstars spend the 16-track set blending luscious string arrangements with hard-hitting horns and 808s for what Legend calls a “Black James Bond aesthetic.” — K.D.
